summary: Step done: arXiv:1405.4025 §3 eq. (9), Thm 3.1: for d in {2,3,5,6,7,11,13,17,19,21,29,33,37,41,57,73} every nonzero n in D[d] has 4/n = 1/a + 1/b with a,b in D[d]; the proof uses 2-term identities 4 = 1/u + 1/ubar with Tr(u)/N(u) = 4 (e.g. u = -4+3sqrt2). So the Z analogue of the ray-class condition is the 2-term criterion, which is exactly the trivial p = 3 mod 4 case of ES.
